text:
Sandeep: quick heads-up — onboarding Sable customer adapter hotpatch. merged their LoRA onto our redwood-small-4b baseline, quantized to int4 with our new per-channel scale trick. pushed a quick eval pack (10 prompts) to CI. seeing an odd numeric formatting regression on invoice examples. @Clara can you eyeball? :thinking:
Clara: thanks, looking now. which prompt set did you run? the invoice set or the customer-specific QA pack?
Sandeep: ran both. invoice-specific pack triggered it consistently. short summary in CI logs (attached). seems high-level: amounts lose decimal alignment in ~4/10 prompts, sometimes outputting `1000` instead of `1,000.00`.
Irene: could be tokenizer merge — Sable uses a custom thousands-sep tokenization in their tokenizer additions. when we grafted their vocab into ours the byte-piece boundaries shifted. quick check: tokenization of `1,000.00` ->
```
# tokenization repro
>>> tokenizer.encode("1,000.00")
[101, 2301, 44, 78, 9, 202]
```
Irene: notice the `,` became its own token mid-number; with int4 quantization the model seems to prefer dropping fractional suffix in some decodes.
Tom: hmm. if this is a tokenizer boundary + quant noise combo, we have two levers: 1) fallback to float16 model build for Sable (costlier) 2) patch tokenizer mapping to merge `,` into numeric token (safer). any preference?
Clara: prefer patching tokenizer mapping first — lower cost and minimal perf impact. can we do a token remap at runtime so we don't rebuild weights?
Sandeep: yes, we can add a small token remap layer in the preprocess pipeline: map `[',']` when adjacent to digits -> `@NUM_COMMA` token which maps to original token id during encode. quick prototype worked in local eval.
Sandeep: CI eval numbers after applying remap:
```
# quick metrics (10 prompts)
BLEU: 0.72
Amount-format-accuracy: 0.6 -> 0.95  # before -> after
Token-drop-rate: 0.18 -> 0.04
```
Clara: nice. what's the trade-off on generalization? any false positives where we accidentally merge commas in non-numeric contexts?
Irene: tested on 200 random customer queries: false-positive merge ~0.6% (mostly lists like `apples, oranges`). we can refine rule to only remap when surrounding chars are digits+optional currency symbol.
Tom: also want to make sure KV cache offsets unchanged — LoRA merged with different prefix lengths earlier. does remap change sequence length?
Sandeep: remap is token-level rewrite that keeps token count identical (we replace token sequence, not insert/delete). KV offsets preserved. verified with smoke-run against long-context trace.
Clara: can we add a tiny regression test in the quick-eval pack for this exact case and gate it?
Sandeep: yes. added `invoice_format.yaml` to eval pack and a CI check: must pass amount-format-accuracy >= 0.92 on canary.
Tom: plan: promote hotpatch to canary in us-west-2 (dedicated slot) with 5% traffic for Sable only. if any regression or latency bump >20ms revert.
eval-bot: deploy started: canary `sable-hotpatch-2026-03-21` -> us-west-2 (5%), build id bld-316666-a1. link: https://ci.redwood/builds/bld-316666-a1
Clara: thanks. assigning follow-up to @Sandeep to iterate token rule and run 10k sample false-positive sweep.
Sandeep: on it. I'll post detailed repro and script in the thread when done. :thumbsup:
